newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan to invest US$350 mln in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Alcan to invest US$350 mln in Brazil.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday that it plans to invest about US$350 million over the next three years to expand and modernize its aluminum rolling operations in Brazil.
The expansion is designed to serve the rapidly growing South American market for aluminum beverage cans, the company said.

Alcan President and Chief Executive Officer Jacques Bougie was to announce the expansion in Ottawa today in the presence of Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who is on a state visit to Canada.

In a two-phase expansion program, Alcan's Brazilian subsidiary, Alcan Aluminio do Brasil S. A. (Alcanbrasil), will more than double production capacity at its Pindamonhangaba aluminum sheet rolling facility to 250,000 tonnes from 100,000 tonnes a year.

The existing Pinda'' plant, with its single-stand hot rolling mill and cold mill, is already Latin America's largest aluminum rolling operation and the only one capable of producing beverage can sheet, Alcan said.
The first step of the expansion will involve the installation of a tandem finishing mill for the existing hot mill, which should be operational within two years.
The second phase will include the addition of a second cold rolling mill and associated equipment, targetted for start-up in 2000.
Alcan said the investment is required to support the development of the aluminum can as a package in South America.

Brazil is the world's third-largest consumer of soft drinks and the sixth-largest consumer of beer. The aluminum can was introduced in Brazil in 1989 and in less than one year replaced steel as the preferred material for beverage cans, Alcan said.
Since then, the can has steadily gained market share on competing beverage containers and, in 1996, nearly 5 billion aluminum cans were used.

Alcan said that in announcing the expansion, it is recognizing the 18% average annual growth rate that is projected for the aluminum can market in Brazil over the next ten years, which will contribute to an overall growth rate of 10% a year for aluminum sheet.

Alcan said that with the expanding can market also comes a growing recycling opportunity for used beverage cans (UBCs), which currently enjoy a recycling rate in Brazil similar to the 63.5% rate seen in the United States.

As part of its Pinda expansion project, Alcanbrasil will construct a 30,000-tonnes-per-year UBC recycling facility that is expected to be operational by the end of 1997, making Alcan the largest UBC recycler in South America, the company said.
